prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset: ONE continuous ground-only outpaint for two vertically adjoining Safety Last game terrain sections.
Input 1 is the EDIT TARGET: a portrait 1666 × 2808 template. Its leftmost 260 pixels are existing ground, and the rest is blank white missing land. Fill the white region with a seamless eastward continuation at the same scale. Preserve the leftmost 132 pixels EXACTLY in place. Input 2 is the PRIMARY style reference for small material scale and hand-painted top-down ground. Input 3 is the geographic guide ONLY: this new strip approaches the eastern works and scrap district; do not render buildings, trees or rails from that overview.

PATH CONNECTIONS ARE CRITICAL. The left reference strip shows TWO incoming routes: a NARROW dirt footpath at about 16% of image height, and a larger rounded-stone path at about 70% of height. Extend both at exactly their existing locations and widths. The upper footpath curves east to join a wider gently winding north–south DIRT service lane around 60% of image width. The lower stone path continues east with matching rounded paving near the contact, then gradually becomes broken scattered paving and broad compacted dirt as it reaches the service lane. Continue a broad dirt branch toward the RIGHT near 68% height. The north–south service lane exits TOP around 65% width and BOTTOM around 57% width. Avoid straight ruler lines and formal symmetrical intersections. Keep open irregular clearings beside these routes for buildings to place separately later.

NEW GROUND: natural transition from the warm left contact into quieter grey-brown and umber compacted earth, irregular darker soil patches, some fine gravel and muted olive/green flat grassy surfaces. Region colours change gradually through irregular ground patterns, never a straight vertical tint boundary. At least 90% of the NEW area has no fallen leaves. Keep only a few tiny local clusters of dull brown leaves near the existing edge. No red/orange leaf carpet, no repeated flower shapes, no carpet of pebbles. Large areas of bare dirt and grass are desirable. New ground must look like the SAME painterly game world, detailed and crisp, with small material marks at the existing scale. Avoid photorealism, blur and huge isolated stones.

Strict top-down flat ground plane, soft neutral overhead light. Ground and paths only. NO buildings, walls, trees, shrubs, raised grass tufts, props, robots, vehicles, fences, rails, water, puddles, large rocks, people, shadows, labels, borders, panels, grids, black fade or white gaps. Preserve incoming path locations and left contact. Output one opaque portrait image, 1666:2808 aspect ratio, highest resolution available, ideally 1666 × 2808 or higher.

Use case: lighting-weather / precise-object-edit.
This image is the EDIT TARGET, a connected ground texture for the same top-down game. Change ONLY the colour of the NEW ground and fine surface shading; preserve every path, paving stone, grass boundary and texture mark in EXACTLY the same position and size. No crop, zoom, camera, object or layout changes.

The leftmost 16% of the image is the fixed existing-map contact: keep that strip completely unchanged. Beyond that edge, transition gradually and irregularly into COOLER, less orange, grey-brown and dark umber industrial-outskirts soil. The rightmost two thirds should be noticeably greyer and deeper brown than now, with some charcoal-brown compacted patches. Warm ochre should remain only near the old left contact and in occasional dirt wear, not as a wash over the entire map. Keep the service tracks readable in muted dusty taupe/tan, NOT bright orange. Grass stays olive-green but slightly more subdued. Use material colour changes, NOT night lighting, dark vignettes, or a uniform grey filter. The soil colour should vary naturally in broad irregular areas.

Do not add or remove objects, paths, stones, grass or leaves. Keep the existing sparse ground and clearings. No new red/orange leaves or flowers. Keep sharp hand-painted texture detail at identical scale, neutral daytime top-down lighting and all artwork to the edge. Output the same portrait composition and aspect ratio at highest available resolution.
